corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc 13; benchmarks/bench_math.c is built by the Makefile bench target at -O3 -march=native (scalar reference and library caller alike); swarm_bench is built with the library CFLAGS -O3 -std=c11 -march=<ISA, default native>; reproduce with make bench and make run-swarm-bench
corrections.caveats: The reduction wins come from multiple SIMD accumulators: the scalar reference (benchmarks/bench_math.c) is a single-accumulator strict-order loop that gcc cannot vectorize without -ffast-math or -fassociative-math, so a hand-unrolled or -ffast-math C loop would close much of the 8.6x/5.1x gap; outputs are not bit-identical to the strict-order loop. bench_math.c times only (best of 200, volatile sink) and does not compare results; swarm_bench does check FP-ASM vs plain C within float reassociation. Memory-bound kernels (axpy, scale) are at parity. Kernel table is one older laptop CPU (i7-4600M); the Emerald Rapids swarm numbers ran with the 100 MB working set in a large L3, and the demo rows under rendering drop to 1.4x total. Young project (1 star, 0 forks).

notes: Numbers on the README match the record exactly (8.6x reduce, 5.1x dot, 1.5x mat4 batch, parity axpy/scale; swarm_bench 7.01 vs 14.48 ms/frame). Benchmark source opened and is honest about using the same -O3 -march=native for the C reference; main shortcoming is that the baseline is a strict-order scalar loop, so the reduction speedups mostly reflect float reassociation. ML-DSA signing has high variance from rejection sampling (clean min 3,322,507 to max 33,055,004 cycles; averages over 1000 runs). m4fstack variants trade speed for stack. SPHINCS+ rows have only a clean C implementation.
